faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in Los Altos Hills?
faq.answer: Los Altos Hills homeowners typically invest $18,000 to $50,000+ for window replacement projects. This exclusive Stanford-adjacent community features large estate homes on 1-acre+ lots, frequently with 20–35 windows and floor-to-ceiling glass walls. Custom sizing and premium hardware are the standard where median home values exceed $5 million. Single window installation starts at approximately $850.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Los Altos Hills?
faq.answer: Yes. Los Altos Hills requires a building permit for all window replacements. The town's Planning and Building Department evaluates projects for consistency with the community's natural, open-space character. Our team manages all permit applications and coordinates with town staff on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in Los Altos Hills?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in Los Altos Hills commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in Los Altos Hills?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most Los Altos Hills replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in Los Altos Hills?
faq.answer: Most Los Altos Hills projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
